'''Marcia Joyce Isakson''' (born 1970, née Geiger, also published as Marcia J. Geiger){{r|straight|diss}} is an American physicist who directs the Signal and Information Sciences Laboratory of the [[J. J. Pickle Research Campus#Research departments|Applied Research Laboratories]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. She is also a former president of the [[Acoustical Society of America]],{{r|hertz}} and holds an affiliate faculty position as a lecturer in the university's Walker Department of Mechanical Engineering.{{r|walker}} Her research concerns modeling and understanding the behavior of [[sonar]] in shallow ocean water, with applications in mapping tidal regions{{r|hertz}} and in national defense.{{r|hertz}}

==Education and career==
Isakson is originally from [[Hereford, Texas]], but moved twice as a teenager to [[Chicago]] and [[Connecticut]],{{r|straight}} where she attended [[New Milford High School (Connecticut)|New Milford High School]].{{r|diss}} She graduated from the [[United States Military Academy]] in [[West Point, New York]] in 1992, with a bachelor's degree in engineering physics and mathematics,{{r|walker}} including an internship at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]].{{r|straight}} After a 1994 master's degree in physics from the University of Texas at Austin, as a Hertz Foundation Fellow,{{r|walker}} and ordnance officer training at the [[Aberdeen Proving Grounds]],{{r|diss}} she became a battalion operations officer in the [[United States Army]] from 1994 to 1997,{{r|walker}} serving as a captain at [[Fort Hood]].{{r|hertz}} Returning to the University of Texas for continued graduate study in physics, she completed her Ph.D. in 2002.{{r|walker}} Her dissertation, ''The Effects of Alignment on the Dissociation of H<sub>2</sub> on Pd(111)'', was advised by Greg Sitz.{{r|diss}}

She joined the Applied Research Laboratories of the University of Texas at Austin in 2001.{{r|walker}} There, she began her work in underwater acoustics, despite her previous physics research being entirely focused on [[laser]]s, [[electromagnetic radiation]],{{r|straight}} and "the dynamics of gas-
surface reactions".{{r|diss}} She also holds a lecturer position in mechanical engineering at the university,{{r|walker}} and taught underwater acoustics there beginning in 2009.{{r|hertz}}

She became president of the Acoustical Society of America for the 2017–2018 term.{{r|pres}} This led her to shift her work at the Applied Research Laboratories from research to management, and in 2021 she became director of the Signal and Information Sciences Laboratory.{{r|straight}}

==Recognition==
Isakson was elected as a Fellow of the [[Acoustical Society of America]] in 2013, "for contributions to modeling shallow water acoustic propagation using the finite element method".{{r|fasa}}

==Personal life==
Isakson is married to John Isakson,{{r|straight}} an electronics engineer and former artillery officer.{{r|john}} They have two children, medical imaging researcher Grace Isakson-Murley and defense software engineering contractor Nicholas Isakson.{{r|straight}}
